newsitem.title: UK: UK'S TBI acquires Florida airport operator.
newsitem.headline: UK'S TBI acquires Florida airport operator.

text.p: British property and airports company TBI Plc announced on Tuesday that it had acquired Central Florida Terminals Inc, which owns and operates Orlando Sanford International Airport in Florida, U.S for an initial consideration of $7 million and a profit-related earn-out.
Orlando Sanford International is the airport facility for non-U.S. passengers arriving at and departing from Sanford which is 12 miles from the centre of Orlando.
TBI said the facility was newly constructed and had opened in April, 1997.
"More than one million passengers were forecast to use the airport in the year to April 30, 1998," TBI said.

TBI will acquire a leasehold interest for a minimum 28 years in the international terminal building as well as the right to market the airport to international operators and to determine and receive all traffic and commercial income.

In return, the freeholder, Sanford Airport Authority, which will be responsible for air traffic control and the upkeep and maintenance of runways, will be entitiled to a rent calculated as a percentage of profits.

TBI would pay the vendors an earn-out over the next 10 years which will be calculated as being up to a maximum of 20 percent of profit before tax in years one five and four percent of PBT in years six to 10.
The amount due to the vendors would be capped at $60 million.
